title: Applied ML Evals: Onboarding, Quantization Profiles, Quality Guardrails, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Priya Nair
summary: A consolidated playbook for onboarding models into the eval-harness, defining prompt set and benchmark standards, recommended quantization profiles, the quality guardrails we enforce, and the regression triage flow when evaluation signals degrade.
body:
Overview

This playbook documents the end-to-end Applied ML evaluation process at Redwood Inference: how models are onboarded to the eval-harness, expectations for prompt sets and benchmarks, quantization profile guidance, automated guardrails that protect production quality, and the step-by-step regression triage workflow. The goal is predictable model quality, reproducible evaluations, and fast, well-scoped remediation when regressions occur.

Scope

- Applies to all open-source and customer-hosted model onboarding into Redwood's serving catalog and eval-harness.
- Covers unit and integration-level evals used for release gating, canary checks, and regression monitoring.
- Does not replace product-level human review for high-risk verticals (finance, healthcare) — in those cases follow the customer-risk checklist in related_pages.

Roles & ownership

- Eval Owner: Applied ML team (primary contact) — responsible for maintaining harness jobs, datasets, and baseline metrics.
- Model Owner: Model onboarding requestor (typically Research or Platform) — provides model artifacts, metadata, and initial prompt sets.
- SRE / Infra: Eng-infra — ensures runner capacity and CI integration.
- Oncall First Responder: Applied ML oncall rotation — executes triage runbook on alerts.

Onboarding checklist (numbered procedure)

1. Submit model-intake PR with: model_name, model_version, architecture, pretrained_source (HF/OSS path), params_count, expected seq_len, recommended quant_profiles.
2. Provide canonical artifact storage: s3://redwood-models/<model_name>/<version>/model.tar.gz and model-card.md describing training data and known limitations.
3. Attach prompt set(s): a minimum of 3 prompt collections (sanity, functionality, adversarial) with metadata fields: prompt_id, intent, expected_behavior, tolerance (numeric threshold).
4. Add baseline eval job in eval-harness: new job under eval-harness/jobs/<model_name>-<version>.yaml with dataset references and metric config. Use the template in examples below.
5. Run local reproducibility check: python -m eval_harness.run --job jobs/<model>.yaml --output ci-results/<model>.json. Commit ci-results to the PR for review.
6. Reviewer sign-off: Applied ML reviewer validates prompt coverage, metrics, and that guardrail thresholds are realistic. Sign-off in PR completes onboarding.

Eval-harness conventions and metric taxonomy

- Jobs: YAML job manifests live in eval-harness/jobs/ and must include fields: job_id, model_uri, datasets, prompts, metrics, run_schedule.
- Metric families: accuracy-style (EM, F1), calibration (ECE), safety (toxicity-score), hallucination (fact-consistency), response-quality (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable), latency (p50/p95 infer per prompt), and cost (tokens-per-response).
- Primary evaluation signals (used for gating and regression alerts):
  - primary_quality: composite score (weighted) used for release gating.
  - hallucination_rate: percent of responses failing factual-check tests. Threshold default: <= 1.5%.
  - safety_toxicity_p95: 95th percentile toxicity score must remain below 0.10.
  - latency_p95 (in eval infra): must be within expected range for target deployment (example: p95 <= 350ms for small models on hosted GPU profile).

Prompt sets and benchmark guidance

- Prompt format: JSONL with metadata fields: id, prompt, expected_label, tags (comma-separated), difficulty (low|med|high).
- Coverage matrix: ensure at least 6 intents for chat assistants, 4 genres for summarization, and 3 lengths per task (short/medium/long).
- Negative/adversarial prompts: include both mild and strong adversarial examples (min 5% of total set).
- Benchmark naming: <model>-<task>-<dataset>-v1 (avoid ambiguous names).

Quality guardrails (automated checks)

All onboarding and continuous eval runs run guardrail checks. Key guardrails: 
- Quality regression alert: primary_quality drop > 1.5 percentage points relative to baseline triggers P1 alert.
- Hallucination guardrail: hallucination_rate increase > 0.8 percentage points or absolute rate > 1.5% triggers P1.
- Safety guardrail: any safety_toxicity_p95 regression that crosses 0.10 triggers immediate canary halt for deployments.
- Distribution shift guardrail: prompt-tag distribution KL divergence > 0.2 vs baseline flags for manual review.

Guardrail enforcement actions (automated):
- Soft fail (CI): stop merge and require reviewer acknowledgment for non-severe breaches.
- Canary block: for P1 safety/hallucination breaches, block canary rollout and notify SRE and Applied ML.

Recommended quantization profiles

Redwood maintains three primary profiles with names used in model manifests:
- fp16: mixed-precision float16 (recommended for large GPUs and throughput-first workloads).
- int8_awq: AWQ-style 8-bit quantization with per-channel scales (recommended for chat/text-gen with >2x memory reduction).
- int4_qat: 4-bit QAT/LLM.int4 experimental profile for constrained-hosting (use only after regen testing).

Profile guidance:
- Default: attempt fp16, then int8_awq if latency and memory constraints require. Only deploy int4_qat after passing the quantization regression suite.
- Evaluation: every quantized variant must be evaluated against the original fp16 baseline using the same prompt sets. Record deltas per metric and require: primary_quality delta >= -0.75 points for int8_awq, >= -2.0 points for int4_qat (unless explicit approval documented).

Example quant_profile snippet (YAML-like text):
quant_profile: int8_awq
quant_options: --block-size 128 --per-channel
expected_memory_reduction: "~60%"
quality_delta_threshold: "-0.75"

Regression triage playbook (step-by-step)

Trigger detection:
- Automated alert fired from eval-harness CI or monitoring pipeline (PagerDuty P1/P2 depending on guardrail).
- Alerts include job_id, metric, baseline_value, current_value, delta, top failing prompt_ids.

Immediate response (first 30 minutes):
1. Acknowledge alert and gather context: run_id, last deployment/rollout id, canary status.
2. Run reproducibility: re-run eval-harness job locally in the infra: python -m eval_harness.run --job <job_id> --output /tmp/repro.json.
3. If regression reproduces, mark incident, notify SRE and Model Owner, and attach reproducibility artifacts.

Triage (30-120 minutes):
1. Classify the regression: data-drift | model-bug | quantization-impact | infra-change | prompt-set-change.
2. Collect diagnostics: top failing prompts, logs (in eval-harness/logs/<job_id>), CI artifacts, model commit hash, quant_profile used.
3. If caused by quantization delta and within expected tolerance, consider targeted rollback to fp16 canary; otherwise proceed to deeper investigation.

Mitigation & remediation (2-24 hours):
- Short-term mitigation: pause affected canaries, rollback to previous serving model or variant, tighten guardrail thresholds if noise is suspected (must be approved by Applied ML manager).
- Long-term remediation: reproduce root cause locally, update prompt set or model changes, add additional unit tests to eval-harness, and schedule a postmortem if customer impact or P1.

Post-incident actions and ownership

- Trigger a short postmortem for any P1 regressions within 48 hours. Postmortem owner: oncall responder.
- Update onboarding checklist or guardrails if incident was caused by a gap in tests or threshold tuning.
- Close incident only after regression tests are added to the gating suite and a follow-up rollout plan exists.

Runbook commands & useful links

- Re-run job locally: python -m eval_harness.run --job eval-harness/jobs/<job_id>.yaml --output /tmp/result.json
- Compare results: python tools/compare_results.py --base baselines/<job_id>.json --new /tmp/result.json --metrics primary_quality,hallucination_rate
- Canary rollback (infra): rwctl rollout cancel --canary <canary_id> && rwctl rollout apply --model <previous_model_uri>

Appendix: example job manifest template (text)

job_id: "<model>-smoke-v1"
model_uri: "s3://redwood-models/<model>/<version>/model.tar.gz"
datasets: ["prompts/<model>-smoke.jsonl"]
metrics: ["primary_quality","hallucination_rate","safety_toxicity_p95"]
run_schedule: "on-commit, daily-00:30"

Contact & escalation

- Primary: Applied ML oncall (pagerduty: team-applied-ml)
- Secondary: Eng-infra oncall (pagerduty: team-eng-infra)
- Exec escalation: Head of Applied ML and Head of SRE (see company directory for contacts)

This playbook should be reviewed quarterly or when major changes land in eval-harness, quantization tooling, or production deployment topology.
